subject: Relaydesk approval scope: corrected requirements and proposed next step
body:
Elise,

Please consider focused refinement of RD-201: make existing review information easier to find from request detail, with relevant activity and reviewer information where an authorized lookup supports it. Before an implementation proposal, Imani and June must agree interaction and recovery examples, Theo must verify activity access and reviewer lookup including missing data, and Theo and June must estimate remaining work. RD-203 is a dependency only where an affected example demonstrates missing contract support.

We have corrected RD-201, RD-203, RD-205 and RD-207 in GitHub and Jira and updated the summer workflow summary. The shared internal explanation and reconciliation are at http://docs.harbor-loom-software.internal/document/doc-1788221338406 . This draft proposes a direction for your review; it makes no implementation or customer-date commitment. The requirements correction is due September 3.

Imani's correspondence review separates one continuing reviewer-discovery case from a different secondhand account about finding an approval in history. The July 21 and August 4 contacts concern the same request, not independent confirmation. The other account still does not establish whether opening the form meant reading or attempting a change. Cedar Reach's automatic department-routing request is separate. We used permitted paraphrases and kept restricted participant identities, correspondence and the permission crosswalk out of shared requirements.

Theo's source comparison shows that the current browser distinguishes Approved, Declined, Waiting for review with an assigned reviewer, and Unassigned. The existing response has a nullable reviewer identifier, which guarantees neither a display name nor reviewer availability. History cannot establish current assignment. The draft state proposal's pending value could collapse waiting and unassigned; it is not deployed behavior. Imani has applied these constraints and missing-lookup, denied-access and load-failure examples to RD-201.

RD-203 remains a contract investigation. Theo retained assigned versus unassigned undecided, imported and conflicting-flag examples, with consumer coexistence, derived versus stored state, transitions and recovery still requiring June and Nolan's review. Old fields remain protected and PR #88 remains draft. A broad redesign is outside this focused visibility refinement.

RD-205 remains a separate investigation into how reviewers are selected, who maintains department routing, missing or unavailable reviewer fallback and any manual override. A permitted concrete example and agreed rules are required before implementation estimates can be trusted.

For RD-207, please confirm the current customer promise once your collection is complete: eligible actors, qualifying conditions, resulting decision and assignment, and retained history, including any account-specific conditions. Petra's two support answers remain unreconciled. Opening a form to read an approval does not establish a right to reopen a declined request. The corrected requirements contain allowed/denied investigation examples without granting unanswered permissions. Theo then assesses enforcement and compatibility; June and Imani assess the interaction and recovery.

All four items retain owners, priorities and unfinished progress. Existing story points are historical planning values, not refreshed estimates. Before proposing a cycle commitment through RD-211, I will reconcile support allowance, Theo's dependency review and RD-212's September 18 maintenance deadline, June's September 4 leave, Imani's two-hour September 3 hiring panel and the September 7 closure. RD-202/PR #87 still needs keyboard-return and empty-result review and an allowance for its remaining work. Numeric remaining capacity and complete frontend estimates are unavailable. No current commitment is displaced by this correction. Any later scope-change proposal will identify what would move out for your decision; Nolan retains production authorization and scheduling.

Workflow reach remains unmeasured. Owen needs a chosen activity and period plus reliable person, account, activity and time records. A possible later analysis could examine opening request detail and consulting approval activity during July 21–August 31, after coverage validation, counting distinct people separately from repeated actions. Missing events do not automatically mean non-use. No export or coverage validation has occurred. The 120-organization/3,500-user census is not approval-workflow reach, and these contacts do not estimate prevalence.

The correction provides a clearer basis for a later scope decision. Interaction review, verified data access, remaining-work estimates, capacity reconciliation and the named business-rule investigations remain open.

Mara
snippet: Elise,Please consider focused refinement of RD-201: make existing review information easier to find
